title: Coalition Success Under Coordinate Polarization
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $b\in\{-1,1\}$, and choose a coordinate $i$. Form the coordinate polarization of $f$ by taking, at inputs with $i$th coordinate $1$, the maximum of the values of $f$ at the two inputs with coordinate $i$ set to $1$ and $-1$, respectively, and taking their minimum when the $i$th coordinate is $-1$. The fraction of inputs from which the coalition $J$ can make the function attain $b$ for this polarized function is at most that fraction for $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
$i$ is a coordinate among the $n$ coordinates
